title: TRADE, TRAVEL, AND TOURISM COMMITTEE REPORT and ADMINISTRATIVE EXEMPTION relative to a Memorandum of Understanding with the Southern California Railway…
text:
[Council File 26-1583; CD 15]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Been Held]
TRADE, TRAVEL, AND TOURISM COMMITTEE REPORT and ADMINISTRATIVE EXEMPTION relative to a Memorandum of Understanding with the Southern California Railway Museum for the loan and public display of an original Port of Los Angeles Waterfront Red Car.
Recommendation(s) for Council action:
1. CONCUR with the determination by the Board of Harbor Commissioners that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines.
2. APPROVE Port of Los Angeles Resolution No. 26-10812 authorizing a Memorandum of Understanding with the Southern California Railway Museum for the loan and public display of original Port of Los Angeles Waterfront Red Car 1058, for a term of 20 years, with two five-year extension options, for a total term not to exceed 30 years.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
The Board of Harbor Commissioners reports that there is no monetary compensation associated with the proposed Memorandum of Understanding. The Harbor Department will be responsible for costs associated with relocating the Red Car to the Southern California Railway Museum. The estimated cost to relocate three Red Cars is $592,218, which will be funded through the 22nd Street Parking Lot Improvement Project. Fiscal Year 2026-27 funding in the amount of $592,218 is available in Account 161305 (Construction in Progress), Division 00000 (Harbor Global), Project 2573900 (208 East 22nd Street Parking Lot Improvements). Neither the City Administrative Officer nor the Chief Legislative Analyst has completed a financial analysis of this report.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
summary: Council would approve a memorandum of understanding lending an original Port of Los Angeles Waterfront Red Car to the Southern California Railway Museum for public display, for 20 years with two five-year extensions. The Harbor Department would cover an estimated $592,218 in relocation costs.
